items.title: Nonempty reward-interface refinements preserve compatibility and monotone reward-function composition
items.author: Rafael Dewes; Rayna Dimitrova
items.source_version: Official published CSL2026.30 CC BY4.0 HTML/PDF Theorem25, complete current AppendixA/B author proofs including Lemmas31/32, retrieved2026-10-14
items.difficulty_reason: The author constructs a new legal environment after a component refinement changes input/output alphabets, proves best-effort implementation preservation using actual inclusion of implementation sets, and builds an infimum-defined reward-threshold comparison function for the composed reward semantics. These constructions must handle hopeful input sequences, projected traces, reward-function monotonicity and universal implementation choices. Both actual supporting proof continuations are retained, supporting H2 as one non-routine compositional refinement theorem rather than splitting its clauses or using sketch-only decision bounds.
